First, we use the product rule for radicals to simplify $\sqrt{80},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{80} & =\sqrt{16\cdot 5}=\sqrt{16}\cdot \sqrt{5}=4\sqrt{5} & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}3\sqrt{80}-8\sqrt{5} & = \\ 3(4\sqrt{5})-8\sqrt{5} & = \\ 12\sqrt{5}-8\sqrt{5}. & \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can combine the two $\sqrt{5}$ terms together:

$$
\begin{aligned}12\sqrt{5}-8\sqrt{5} & = \\ (12-8)\sqrt{5} & = \\ 4\sqrt{5} & \end{aligned}
$$
